```{=html}
<div style="margin-bottom: 20px; padding: 18px 22px; border: 2px solid navy; border-radius: 8px; background: #ffffff; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.05);">
  <h3 style="color: navy; margin-top: 0;">Exploring the Night Sky: Constellation Line Graphs</h3>
  <p style="margin-bottom: 8px; color: #333;">
    For thousands of years, humans have connected the dots between distant stars to create mythological figures, navigation guides, and seasonal calendars.
    Below is an interactive constellation chart mapping major constellations across the celestial sphere.
  </p>
  <p style="margin: 0; font-size: 14px; color: #555;">
    💡 <strong>Tip:</strong> Hover over any star to inspect its name, magnitude, distance, and spectral color. Click on constellation names in the legend to toggle them on or off!
  </p>
</div>
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

# Define stars with celestial coordinates (RA in hours converted to deg, Dec in deg),
# visual magnitude, distance in ly, color, and lore.
stars_data <- tribble(
  ~star, ~constellation, ~ra_deg, ~dec_deg, ~mag, ~dist_ly, ~color_hex, ~spectral, ~lore,
  # Orion (The Hunter)
  "Betelgeuse", "Orion", 88.79, 7.41, 0.5, 548, "#ff7043", "M1-2 Ia-ab (Red Supergiant)", "Right shoulder; pulsing red supergiant nearing supernova.",
  "Rigel", "Orion", 78.63, -8.20, 0.18, 860, "#90caf9", "B8 Ia (Blue Supergiant)", "Left foot; luminous blue supergiant, 120,000x brighter than Sun.",
  "Bellatrix", "Orion", 81.28, 6.35, 1.64, 250, "#bbdefb", "B2 III (Blue Giant)", "Left shoulder; known as the Amazon Star.",
  "Saiph", "Orion", 86.94, -9.67, 2.07, 650, "#bbdefb", "B0.5 Ia (Supergiant)", "Right foot of the cosmic hunter.",
  "Alnitak", "Orion", 85.19, -1.94, 1.74, 1260, "#90caf9", "O9.7 Ib (Blue Supergiant)", "Eastern star of Orion's Belt; near Flame & Horsehead nebulae.",
  "Alnilam", "Orion", 84.05, -1.20, 1.69, 2000, "#90caf9", "B0 Ia (Blue Supergiant)", "Center star of Orion's Belt.",
  "Mintaka", "Orion", 83.00, -0.30, 2.25, 1200, "#90caf9", "O9.5 II (Bright Giant)", "Western star of Orion's Belt, closely aligned with celestial equator.",

  # Ursa Major (Big Dipper)
  "Dubhe", "Ursa Major", 165.93, 61.75, 1.79, 123, "#ffcc80", "K0 III (Orange Giant)", "Pointers star pointing directly towards Polaris.",
  "Merak", "Ursa Major", 165.46, 56.38, 2.37, 79, "#ffffff", "A1 V (White)", "Lower pointer star of the Dipper's bowl.",
  "Phecda", "Ursa Major", 178.46, 53.69, 2.44, 83, "#ffffff", "A0 V (White)", "Bottom-inner bowl star of the Big Dipper.",
  "Megrez", "Ursa Major", 183.86, 57.03, 3.32, 80, "#ffffff", "A3 V (White)", "Junction joining the bowl to the handle.",
  "Alioth", "Ursa Major", 193.51, 55.96, 1.76, 82, "#ffffff", "A1 III-IV (White)", "Brightest star in Ursa Major; base of the handle.",
  "Mizar", "Ursa Major", 200.98, 54.92, 2.23, 83, "#ffffff", "A2 V (White)", "Famous double star with companion Alcor, used in ancient eyesight tests.",
  "Alkaid", "Ursa Major", 206.89, 49.31, 1.85, 103, "#bbdefb", "B3 V (Blue-White)", "Tip of the Dipper handle; name means Leader of the Daughters.",

  # Cassiopeia (The Queen)
  "Caph", "Cassiopeia", 2.30, 59.15, 2.28, 55, "#fff9c4", "F2 III (Yellow-White)", "Western star of the celestial 'W'.",
  "Schedar", "Cassiopeia", 10.13, 56.54, 2.24, 228, "#ffb74d", "K0 IIIa (Orange Giant)", "Heart of Queen Cassiopeia.",
  "Gamma Cas", "Cassiopeia", 14.18, 60.72, 2.15, 550, "#90caf9", "B0.5 IVe (Blue Variable)", "Center peak of the 'W'; violent rapid rotator.",
  "Ruchbah", "Cassiopeia", 20.20, 60.23, 2.68, 99, "#ffffff", "A5 V (White)", "Knee of the seated queen.",
  "Segin", "Cassiopeia", 26.60, 63.67, 3.35, 460, "#bbdefb", "B3 III (Blue Giant)", "Eastern tip of the 'W'.",

  # Cygnus (The Swan / Northern Cross)
  "Deneb", "Cygnus", 310.29, 45.28, 1.25, 2615, "#ffffff", "A2 Ia (White Supergiant)", "Tail of the swan; corner of the Summer Triangle.",
  "Sadr", "Cygnus", 305.56, 40.26, 2.23, 1800, "#fff9c4", "F8 Ib (Supergiant)", "Chest of the Swan; intersection of the Northern Cross.",
  "Albireo", "Cygnus", 291.80, 27.96, 3.05, 430, "#ffa726", "K2 II + B8 V (Gold & Blue)", "Beak of the swan; famous striking color binary.",
  "Gienah", "Cygnus", 311.55, 33.97, 2.48, 73, "#ffcc80", "K0 III (Giant)", "Eastern wing of the Swan.",
  "Fawaris", "Cygnus", 296.24, 45.13, 2.86, 165, "#bbdefb", "B9.5 III (Blue-White)", "Western wing of the Swan.",

  # Canis Major (The Great Dog)
  "Sirius", "Canis Major", 101.29, -16.72, -1.46, 8.6, "#e0f7fa", "A1 V (Bright White)", "Brightest star in Earth's night sky; the Dog Star.",
  "Mirzam", "Canis Major", 95.68, -17.96, 1.98, 500, "#90caf9", "B1 II-III (Blue Giant)", "Announcer star rising just before Sirius.",
  "Wezen", "Canis Major", 107.10, -26.39, 1.83, 1600, "#fff9c4", "F8 Ia (Yellow-White Supergiant)", "Weight/rump of the Great Dog.",
  "Adhara", "Canis Major", 104.66, -28.97, 1.50, 430, "#90caf9", "B2 II (Blue Bright Giant)", "One of the brightest ultraviolet emitters in the sky.",
  "Aludra", "Canis Major", 110.96, -29.30, 2.45, 2000, "#90caf9", "B5 Ia (Blue Supergiant)", "Tail tip of the Great Dog."
)

# Constellation lines connecting stars
connections <- tribble(
  ~constellation, ~from, ~to,
  # Orion
  "Orion", "Betelgeuse", "Bellatrix",
  "Orion", "Betelgeuse", "Alnitak",
  "Orion", "Bellatrix", "Mintaka",
  "Orion", "Mintaka", "Alnilam",
  "Orion", "Alnilam", "Alnitak",
  "Orion", "Alnitak", "Saiph",
  "Orion", "Mintaka", "Rigel",
  "Orion", "Saiph", "Rigel",

  # Ursa Major
  "Ursa Major", "Dubhe", "Merak",
  "Ursa Major", "Merak", "Phecda",
  "Ursa Major", "Phecda", "Megrez",
  "Ursa Major", "Megrez", "Dubhe",
  "Ursa Major", "Megrez", "Alioth",
  "Ursa Major", "Alioth", "Mizar",
  "Ursa Major", "Mizar", "Alkaid",

  # Cassiopeia
  "Cassiopeia", "Caph", "Schedar",
  "Cassiopeia", "Schedar", "Gamma Cas",
  "Cassiopeia", "Gamma Cas", "Ruchbah",
  "Cassiopeia", "Ruchbah", "Segin",

  # Cygnus
  "Cygnus", "Deneb", "Sadr",
  "Cygnus", "Sadr", "Albireo",
  "Cygnus", "Fawaris", "Sadr",
  "Cygnus", "Sadr", "Gienah",

  # Canis Major
  "Canis Major", "Mirzam", "Sirius",
  "Canis Major", "Sirius", "Wezen",
  "Canis Major", "Wezen", "Adhara",
  "Canis Major", "Wezen", "Aludra"
)

# Convert magnitude to marker size (brighter = lower mag = larger dot)
stars_data <- stars_data |> 
  mutate(
    size_px = scales::rescale(-mag, to = c(7, 18)),
    hover_info = paste0(
      "<b>", star, "</b> (", constellation, ")<br>",
      "<b>Visual Mag:</b> ", mag, "<br>",
      "<b>Distance:</b> ", dist_ly, " ly<br>",
      "<b>Class:</b> ", spectral, "<br>",
      "<em>", lore, "</em>"
    )
  )

# Build plotly figure
fig <- plot_ly()

# Add constellation stick figure lines
constellations_list <- unique(connections$constellation)
palette <- c(
  "Orion" = "#ff9800",
  "Ursa Major" = "#00e5ff",
  "Cassiopeia" = "#e040fb",
  "Cygnus" = "#76ff03",
  "Canis Major" = "#ffd600"
)

for (con in constellations_list) {
  con_lines <- connections |> filter(constellation == con)
  
  # Build line segments with NA breaks
  seg_x <- c()
  seg_y <- c()
  
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(con_lines))) {
    f_star <- stars_data |> filter(star == con_lines$from[i])
    t_star <- stars_data |> filter(star == con_lines$to[i])
    
    seg_x <- c(seg_x, f_star$ra_deg, t_star$ra_deg, NA)
    seg_y <- c(seg_y, f_star$dec_deg, t_star$dec_deg, NA)
  }
  
  col <- palette[con]
  
  fig <- fig |> 
    add_trace(
      x = seg_x,
      y = seg_y,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "lines",
      name = paste0(con, " (Lines)"),
      line = list(color = col, width = 2, dash = "solid"),
      hoverinfo = "none",
      showlegend = FALSE
    )
}

# Add star nodes for each constellation
for (con in constellations_list) {
  con_stars <- stars_data |> filter(constellation == con)
  col <- palette[con]
  
  fig <- fig |> 
    add_trace(
      data = con_stars,
      x = ~ra_deg,
      y = ~dec_deg,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "markers+text",
      name = con,
      text = ~star,
      textposition = "top center",
      textfont = list(color = "#ffffff", size = 11),
      hoverinfo = "text",
      hovertext = ~hover_info,
      marker = list(
        size = ~size_px,
        color = ~color_hex,
        line = list(color = col, width = 1.5),
        opacity = 0.95
      )
    )
}

fig <- fig |> 
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = "Celestial Constellations Sky Map",
      font = list(color = "navy", size = 17)
    ),
    plot_bgcolor = "#080d1a",
    paper_bgcolor = "#ffffff",
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Right Ascension (Degrees)",
      zeroline = FALSE,
      gridcolor = "#152238",
      autorange = "reversed" # Sky maps traditionally display East to the left (reversed RA)
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Declination (Degrees)",
      zeroline = TRUE,
      zerolinecolor = "#2c3e50",
      gridcolor = "#152238"
    ),
    legend = list(
      orientation = "h",
      x = 0.05,
      y = 1.12,
      font = list(color = "#333", size = 12)
    ),
    margin = list(t = 70, b = 50, l = 50, r = 30)
  )

fig
```

```{=html}
<div style="margin-top: 30px; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)); gap: 16px;">
  <div style="padding: 16px; border: 1px solid #e0e0e0; border-radius: 8px; background: #fafafa; border-top: 4px solid #ff9800;">
    <h4 style="margin: 0 0 8px 0; color: #e65100;">🏹 Orion (The Hunter)</h4>
    <p style="margin: 0; font-size: 13.5px; line-height: 1.5; color: #424242;">
      Anchored by red supergiant Betelgeuse and blazing blue Rigel, Orion is one of the most recognized constellations on Earth. Its three belt stars point directly towards Sirius.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div style="padding: 16px; border: 1px solid #e0e0e0; border-radius: 8px; background: #fafafa; border-top: 4px solid #00e5ff;">
    <h4 style="margin: 0 0 8px 0; color: #00838f;">🐻 Ursa Major (Big Dipper)</h4>
    <p style="margin: 0; font-size: 13.5px; line-height: 1.5; color: #424242;">
      The Great Bear contains the famous Big Dipper asterism. Its outer bowl stars, Merak and Dubhe, act as cosmic pointers leading navigators directly to Polaris (the North Star).
    </p>
  </div>

  <div style="padding: 16px; border: 1px solid #e0e0e0; border-radius: 8px; background: #fafafa; border-top: 4px solid #e040fb;">
    <h4 style="margin: 0 0 8px 0; color: #8e24aa;">👑 Cassiopeia (The Queen)</h4>
    <p style="margin: 0; font-size: 13.5px; line-height: 1.5; color: #424242;">
      Recognizable by its distinctive 'W' or 'M' shape in northern skies, Cassiopeia orbits opposite the Big Dipper around the celestial pole.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div style="padding: 16px; border: 1px solid #e0e0e0; border-radius: 8px; background: #fafafa; border-top: 4px solid #76ff03;">
    <h4 style="margin: 0 0 8px 0; color: #2e7d32;">🦢 Cygnus (The Northern Cross)</h4>
    <p style="margin: 0; font-size: 13.5px; line-height: 1.5; color: #424242;">
      Flying along the Milky Way's galactic plane, Cygnus features supergiant Deneb at its tail and the stunning colored binary star Albireo at its beak.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div style="padding: 16px; border: 1px solid #e0e0e0; border-radius: 8px; background: #fafafa; border-top: 4px solid #ffd600;">
    <h4 style="margin: 0 0 8px 0; color: #f57f17;">🐕 Canis Major (The Great Dog)</h4>
    <p style="margin: 0; font-size: 13.5px; line-height: 1.5; color: #424242;">
      Home to Sirius, the brightest star in Earth's night sky at only 8.6 light-years away, faithfully trailing behind Orion across the winter skies.
    </p>
  </div>
</div>
```
